title: Russell Brand sentenced to more than 10 years for rape and sexual assault offences – as it happened
description:
Disgraced comedian must serve two-thirds of the 10 years and six month sentence before he will be eligible for parole

  • Russell Brand sentenced to more than 10 years in prison

Proceedings are beginning now. Chief prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones KC is up on her feet. She’ll be the first to deliver remarks.

The sentencing has been pushed back as court staff attempt to rearrange the courtroom so one of the victims can be protected, PA reports.

Continue reading...
text: Brand sentenced to 10 years and six months for rape and sexual assault offences
Judge Bennathan asks Brand to stand up as he passes his sentence judgment.
He says the sentence for rape is nine years imprisonment.
The total sentence is 10 years, six months, with the sexual assault offences.
The judge gave prison sentences of nine months, 18 months, and eight months for those three offences.
Prosecutors had called for the judge to mete out a sentence of this severity, for a category one penalty which ranges from 10-15 years.

We’re still getting reaction coming through in response to the sentencing but I’m going to leave it for there. I’ll recap what we saw in court today.

Firstly, the top line: Russell Brand, one of Britain’s most high-profile former actor-comedians, the star of several Hollywood films in the 2000s and 2010s, has been jailed to a total of 10-and-a-half years for rape and sexual assault crimes against four women.
Brand was found guilty last Thursday by a jury made up of eight men and four women. They convicted him of offences against four women in separate incidents from 2004-2009.

The rape took place at his home address in Hampstead, London while the three other sexual assaults – where Brand forcefully kissed, groped and assaulted the women- took place in a Soho bar in central London, a Channel 4 radio studio and a Capital Radio building. Brand was also accused of two other rape counts and an attempted indecent assault, but cleared of those charges.
This morning, Justice Joel Bennathan heard arguments from Brand’s lawyer and the prosecutor as to the severity of his punishment.

Brand’s lawyer asked the judge for mercy, saying Brand was a changed man these days and had a young family. Ian Winter KC also said the four crimes were all “isolated incidents” and the rape “a short and momentary failure”.
The crown prosecutor said Brand was a ruthless predator who used his fame to relentlessly use women to fulfil his sexual desires

Reil Karmy-Jones KC asked for the judge to hand down the most serious level of sentencing, because Brand had caused severe psychological harm to his rape victim and also subjected her to degrading, humiliating treatment

The prosecution read out the victim impact statements where all the women described the debilitating impact of Brand’s assault and abuse on their life. One of the victims came to court to deliver her remarks.
Shortly after 2pm, Judge Bennathan delivered his sentencing decision. He repeatedly called Brand a sexual predator, who had used his fame and power to carry out crimes and protect himself.
His crimes showed the “belief that fame meant you could act however you liked, when you liked, unhindered by the rules by which decent people live.”
He also said the offences, often committed in public, showed Brand’s “staggering arrogance” and that an entourage around Brand “indulged” in the “dreadful behaviour”.

The judge said: “Whatever women wear, wherever they go, indeed whatever they drink, they retain the right to say no and to demand justice from the criminal courts when sexual predators like you, Russell Brand, act without their consent.”
He sentenced Brand to nine years imprisonment for the rape conviction
He sentenced Brand to nine months, 18 months and eight months for the sexual assaults
In total, Brand has been jailed to 10.5 years in prison. He will be eligible for parole in 2032.
His lengthy sentence has been welcomed by police and prosecutors who have urged all victims of sexual assault and rape to report such crimes to authorities.
Russell Brand has been jailed today to more than 10 years for raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others.
All of them gave victim impact statements to the court, all of which were read out today for the judge to hear as he considered the punishment he would give to Brand.

One woman also chose to come into the courtroom to deliver her remarks directly to the judge. The court put up screens and drew a curtain at that point to protect her anonymity – so that she couldn’t be seen by Brand and was only seen by the judge, who thanked her for her courage in “in front of so many people”.
I’ve recounted throughout the blog the statements of all four women, but you can also read them here:
Justice Joel Bennathan delivered an eight-page judgement at the sentencing today.
The punishment – the full length of the prison term Russell Brand will serve for the next 10 years– was delivered right at the end in the 80-second clip below. You can watch it here.
Brand spoke to wife as he was taken away
The court drawing below depicts how Brand spoke to his wife Laura Brand as he was led away to the cells.
After the 10.5 year sentence was passed, Ms Brand told her husband “I love you”.
He said to her as he was being taken out: “We’ll be okay.”
Ms Brand left the courtroom in tears. The couple have three children together, the eldest aged 10.
Senior crown prosecutor David Roberts spoke after Det Supt Furphy, and said that:
double quotation markToday’s result shows that fame, status, and a passage of time do not change the fundamental issue of consent.

He says the evidence presented to court showed Brand to be a “manipulative sexual predator, using his growing fame and power to create situations in which he could pursue women sexually, regardless of what they wanted, with complete disregard for the impact of his actions”.
He also began his remarks by praising the victims.
double quotation markThey did not know each other, and each of them has carried what happened to them for almost two decades.
Police and prosecutors urge all rape and sexual assault victims to come forward
Furphy commends the work of police and their support for the female victim and then makes a final, direct appeal “to anyone who’s been a victim of rape or any other sexual offence.

double quotation markWe know it can take enormous courage to speak about what happened to you. No matter how long ago it occurred, or who was responsible, if you come forward, you’ll be listened to, supported, and treated with care and compassion.
Russell Brand, once a Hollywood film star and award-winning comedian, has just been sentenced to over 10 years in jail for sexual assault and rape crimes he committed two decades ago.
Some of the women in their victim impact statements, read out in court today, said they hadn’t discussed what had happened to them with other people, sometimes for 20 years.
But they had felt emboldened to come forward to police following investigations published by The Times, Sunday Times and Channel 4 in 2023 concerning allegations made by other women.

Met Police since last Thursday have said they are also investigating two other rape allegations against Brand, including one involving a then 16-year-old girl, and have passed on those cases to prosecutors.
Police: 'Russell Brand has been held accountable for his crimes'

The lead detective on the case, Det Supt Andy Furphy, has just spoken outside the courtroom saying today’s sentence is a significant milestone, one that “means Russell Brand has been held accountable for his crimes.”
He goes on to praise the six women who bravely came forward and endured court interrogation to get to where we are today.
“I hope they recognise just how powerful their actions have been and the difference they may make to others,” says Furphy.
Full comments below:

double quotation markMy thoughts today are with the women who came forward and made this investigation possible. Reporting sexual offences can be incredibly difficult and they have shown immense bravery, dignity, and resilience throughout what has been a lengthy and challenging trial process. The victims have had to revisit deeply traumatic experiences and endure significant public and media attention. I hope today’s outcome provides some measure of closure, and allows them to continue rebuilding their lives. Their courage in coming forward has not only led to this outcome, but may also give confidence to others who have suffered sexual violence, to seek help and report what happened to them. I hope they recognise just how powerful their actions have been and the difference they may make to others. From the very beginning, our investigation was never about Russell Brand’s profile, status, or celebrity. Our focus has always been on the women who reported these offences, and on conducting a thorough and impartial investigation into the allegations that they made.
Judge added two years to rape sentence for Brand removing condom and other serious aggravating factors
Regarding the rape sentencing, Judge Bennathan noted that Brand ordering the then 21-year-old woman to “clean your sheets” was “an additional… humiliation”.
He also said that Brand removing the condom without her consent, and ejaculating into her “which led to months of fearing she might have HIV” were “serious further aggravating factors”.
He said those actions “must raise” his sentence punishment by two years above the starting point.
As I reported earlier, the judge reduced the sentence by one year for mitigating factors such as Brand not having any serious prior convictions.

These are the details of the rape conviction, where Brand in 2009 anally raped a 21-year-old fan of his, removed the condom and ejaculated in her, humiliated her afterwards and left her terrified that she might have contracted HIV.
The judge summarised the crime as following:

double quotation markShe was a huge fan of yours, which you were happy to exploit. She had willing consensual sexual activity with you after your show. You took her phone number and if anyone still needs any demonstration of your contempt for your casual sexual partners, you stored her number under “T” for “tart”. You invited her to your house a few days later. There you put on a condom at her request and had vaginal sex, to which she consented. You then flipped her over, removed the condom and, without asking, forced your penis into her anus, causing her great pain. She asked you to stop, then asked you again loudly. You replied, and I quote, “I want you to feel my cum”. You ejaculated. She was distraught and in severe pain. The bed was heavily soiled by blood, sperm and faeces. You told her it was her mess, and made her try to clear it up. Shortly after, you went off to get ready then went to work. She was driven to a nearby underground station by your driver who for some reason had tissues ready, to hand to her as she wept. She was left distraught, in pain and terrified she might have contracted HIV.
Judge Bennathan noted how Brand’s actions had caused “significant and long-lasting” harm to the woman.

double quotation markIn her victim impact statement she wrote of struggling to eat and sleep, of taking two to three months off from work and of abandoning the career she had embarked upon. Although the rape was 17 years ago, she still finds it affects her ability to form new friendships and to know when she can trust people. From her evidence at trial I also know she developed an alcohol problem, partly as a result of your attack on her.
Russell Brand was sentenced to nine years for the rape conviction alone.
He was acquitted of two other rape counts, but because of this count, has received such a serious sentence behind bars.
Judge Bennathan went into length on this offence, and I will get into that in the next post.
The judge had said he was “very conscious” that Brand’s imprisonment would “deprive your children of the presence of their father”.
double quotation markThat sad loss to them, however, is caused by your serious offending.
Brand’s lawyer Ian Winter KC earlier had strenuously made the case that a lengthy sentence would have a “catastrophic” impact on Brand’s wife and three children.
Brand was taken into custody immediately after a jury found him guilty last Thursday so has not had the opportunity to say goodbye in person to his family.
Judge Bennathan also commended the Met Police for “their hard work in gathering evidence and taking great care of all the women who testified.”
As I reported earlier, one of the victims said she had wanted to withdraw her case after the stress and pressure and public attention, but she persisted with the support of specialist police teams.
The Met Police have said they expect other women may come forward to report their experiences of abuse and assault.
